Title: April 16, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
Overview: The April 16, 2026 regular meeting opened with resident comments on topics including airport operations, recreation center funding, and surveillance technology, then moved through the consent agenda, which council approved unanimously. The main business was metropolitan districts: council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8748, which limits district formation to mostly commercial areas and sets debt and levy caps, but deferred the model service plan resolution so staff can add a compounding interest option. Council also reviewed state legislation and agreed to take an oppose-unless-amended position on House Bill 1308 on lot splitting.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke during open comment on a range of issues including the transportation maintenance fee exemption for religious buildings, zoning and landmarking reviews, the Boulder Municipal Airport, South Boulder Rec Center funding, bear trash ordinance evaluation, tipped minimum wage, and Flock AI surveillance. Speakers were limited to two or three minutes and staff and council responded briefly to several comments. Council members asked residents to direct criticism at policies rather than individuals or staff.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda items 3A through 3I unanimously. Questions covered the Spring Valley Estates annexation water lines and resident cost sharing, and Ordinance 8745 on land use code changes, where staff kept the original three-story recommendation rather than the planning board's alteration. Council also discussed a brewery square footage issue to be researched.

Topic3.Title: Metropolitan Districts Ordinance 8748 and Model Service Plan
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented the regulatory framework for metropolitan districts, which limits formation to commercial districts with at least 90 percent non-residential use, sets a 50 mill debt cap and 65 mill aggregate cap, and imposes a 40-year debt discharge rule and a three-mill regional improvements levy. Council questioned the mill levy impacts, voter eligibility, and compounding interest. Council then adopted Ordinance 8748 unanimously, and the model service plan resolution was deferred so staff can add a compounding interest option.

Topic4.Title: Legislative Update and State Advocacy
Topic4.Summary: Intergovernmental affairs staff reviewed the state legislative session, including House Bill 1202 on homelessness, Senate Bill 148 on on-bill energy repayment, AI policy, budget cuts, and the Home Act. Council discussed Senate Bill 150 on RTD reform and House Bill 1308 on lot splitting, and agreed to take an oppose-unless-amended position on 1308 that would move to monitor if three requested amendments are adopted. Council also received a note on a staff award.
